legal.contextNote: The Supreme Court Registry’s notice (dated 3 Nov 2026) flags the domain scigovinjudicial.com as a phishing site impersonating the Court’s official portal. No precedent directly on Supreme Court‑issued phishing alerts; the closest case law is *Shreya Singhal v. Union of India* (2015) upholding the validity of Section 66A (now repealed) for online harassment, indicating courts’ willingness to intervene against misuse of digital platforms.

legal.headline: Can AI be a co-mediator? Experts at IMF’s ‘An evening with mediators’ discuss future of mediation in India

legal.summary: Experts at IMF’s ‘An Evening with Mediators’ discuss the future of mediation in India, highlighting institutional reforms, AI integration, professionalisation and the need to build a trusted mediation ecosystem At the Indian Mediation Federation’s (IMF) ‘An Evening with Mediators’, held on 31 October 2026 in New Delhi, a panel discussion brought together experienced mediators and legal professionals to examine the practical changes needed to strengthen India’s mediation ecosystem. The discussion moved beyond the question of recognising mediation as an alternative to litigation to explore how institutional reforms, professional expertise and technological innovation could make mediation a more accessible, credible and trusted process.
legal.contextNote: The Indian Mediation Federation (IMF) hosted ‘An Evening with Mediators’ on 31 Oct 2026 in New Delhi. The panel, featuring senior mediators and corporate lawyers, argued for statutory reforms, a dedicated Mediation Act amendment, and the integration of AI tools for case triage and outcome prediction. They cited the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (Section 89) as the current legal basis for court‑referenced mediation and urged a separate AI‑governance framework under the Draft Data Protection Bill (DPDP Act). No court judgment or regulator order is cited; the discussion is purely policy‑driven.

opinion.headline: Firm It Up, Don't Junk It: India needs a more predictable capital gains tax regime to deepen equity markets

opinion.summary: India's capital markets have seen significant changes, with millions of households participating in equity investing. The current tax framework needs to evolve to encourage better investment behavior among participants. A predictable and neutral tax system can foster deeper domestic participation in capital markets. It proposes a graduated CGT structure to align tax with investment horizons and deepen market participation. No specific case law is cited; the article is an editorial call for legislative reform.
